A Morgan Stanley (MS) report dated September 16, 2026, analyzes early demand signals for the iPhone 18 Pro/Pro Max. Despite market concerns that a price hike would suppress demand, the report highlights a key observation: while Pro model production is estimated to be up 18% year-over-year (71M vs. 60M units), global average delivery lead times have remained essentially flat. MS interprets this stability in lead times amid a significant supply increase as a sign of healthy concurrent demand strength, providing a more positive early signal than feared.

Notably, delivery times in markets like the US, Japan, UK, France, and Germany were stable or slightly longer, which MS considers more representative. China was the exception, showing shorter lead times attributed to local competition and demand patterns. MS acknowledges two potential demand suppressants: the later launch of the iPhone Duo (causing some to wait) and the $100 price increase. The fact that lead times held steady despite these headwinds is seen as meaningful. Factors supporting demand include increased carrier subsidies (e.g., +$100 in the US) and a growing installed base.

MS maintains an Overweight rating on Apple with a $360 price target (~8.7% upside from $331.34).
